matches.rationale: Both identify the same internal contradiction regarding whether ALFAR is training-free or involves training/fine-tuning. The ground truth notes an Abstract-vs-Method inconsistency about training, while Finding 1 captures a direct contradiction within the Abstract itself about training-free vs. light training—the core scientific issue of misrepresented training requirements is the same.

Ground truth identifies a specific mathematical flaw in Equation (11)'s asymmetric fusion formula that can produce negative weights. None of the findings address Equation (11) or the logit fusion formula at all; Finding 3 addresses attention reallocation (Equation 5-7), not logit fusion.

Ground truth describes unfair experimental comparison due to asymmetric GPU resources and batch sizes favoring ALFAR. None of the findings mention GPU allocation, batch size asymmetry, or resource unfairness in experiments.

Both identify manipulation of ALFAR's performance numbers in Table 2 by 3-5%. The ground truth says numbers are boosted, while Finding 2 notes the caption states 'overall gains reduced by 3-5%'—both capture the same underlying issue of numerical manipulation in the reported Table 2 results.

Ground truth concerns overclaiming robustness in Discussion by failing to qualify ambiguous/incorrect example responses. Finding 5 identifies a text-figure mismatch in Section 6.5 (performance decline vs. qualitative Fig. 6). These are different scientific issues—exaggerated claims vs. wrong figure reference.
Ground truth identifies missing IRB approvals, consent, and privacy safeguards in Acknowledgments. No finding addresses ethical compliance omissions or the Acknowledgments section.

Ground truth identifies references citing 2025+ papers beyond knowledge cutoff with imaginary authors. Finding 4 addresses a different citation issue—misattribution of GPT-3.5 to an InstructGPT paper [72]—not future-dated or fabricated references.

Ground truth flags promotional rhetoric in Introduction ('fully exploits,' 'superior performance by large margins'). No finding addresses rhetorical tone or overclaiming language in the Introduction section.

Ground truth identifies a specific numeric contradiction near Figure 1 between text and figure regarding ALFAR vs. MRAG performance on 2nd/3rd retrieved knowledge rankings. Finding 5 addresses a different figure-text mismatch (Fig. 6 in Section 6.5), not Figure 1.

Ground truth describes heterogeneous baseline comparisons with different model sizes/architectures lacking normalization. None of the findings address baseline heterogeneity or missing normalization in experiments.

Ground truth identifies a cross-section conflict: Section 6.3 claims scalability while Section 6.5 shows performance decline in larger models. Finding 5 addresses a different issue within Section 6.5—a figure-text mismatch where performance decline is attributed to a qualitative figure (Fig. 6)—not the cross-section coherence problem.
Ground truth notes omission of bias evaluations and safety analyses for knowledge bases (Wikipedia, GPT-3.5 generated). No finding addresses missing bias/safety evaluation in the experimental setup.

Ground truth identifies misattribution of the GPT-4 technical report to incorrect venue ([71]). Finding 4 identifies misattribution of GPT-3.5 to an InstructGPT paper ([72]). While both involve GPT-related citation errors, they target different specific references, different sections (References vs. Appendix A5), and different underlying papers, making them distinct issues.
Ground truth identifies selective rhetoric in Conclusion that omits limitations and overstates maturity. No finding addresses the Conclusion section or its omission of limitations.

Ground truth identifies selective citation in Related Work that neglects recent training-free fusion techniques, biasing novelty claims. No finding addresses the Related Work section or selective citation omissions there.

Ground truth identifies that attention reallocation formulas (Eq. 5) modify weights without preserving causal masks, risking autoregressive constraint violations. Finding 3 identifies a different issue with the same formulas—a mismatch between the claimed use of retrieval similarity α and the actual equations using γ_j = k·ω_j. These are distinct scientific problems.
